ms.promise:
Context: UPLC converter is a CLI tool to be integrated with Cardano on-chain language tools so that smart contract developers can create zero-knowledge smart contracts using the familiar smart contract languages.

Task: We develop a prototype that works with a subset of UPLC (some language constructions are not allowed and a limited number of builtins supported).
・Implement a prototype for a limited subset of UPLC (Haskell)
・Implement a comprehensive test suite (Haskell)

Outputs:
・A prototype for a limited subset of UPLC (Haskell)
・A comprehensive test suite (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
In terms of the builtin operations, the prototype will be limited to arithmetic and comparison operations on integers, comparison operations on bytestrings, and the “IfThenElse” operation. It will also use the November 2022 spec for UPLC instead of the latest one. We validate the prototype by comparing the result of UPLC script execution against the result of the execution of the corresponding arithmetic circuit.
・A prototype for a limited subset of UPLC (Haskell) can be found in our repo
・A comprehensive test suite (Haskell) can be found in our repo
ms.report:
We have developed a prototype that works with a subset of UPLC and comprehensive test suites:
A prototype for a limited subset of UPLC (Haskell):
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/zkfold-uplc/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/UPLC/Converter.hs#L33

https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/pull/359
In addition, please see a video explaining the prototype and demo showcasing the prototype converting the UPLC for ease of verification:

As requested, we have added a comprehensive video to YouTube explaining all the details:

ms.promise:
Context: UPLC converter is a CLI tool to be integrated with Cardano on-chain language tools so that smart contract developers can create zero-knowledge smart contracts using the familiar smart contract languages.
Task: We develop arithmetic circuits for the set of basic builtin operations (cryptographic operations and serialization are excluded).
Outputs: 
・Arithmetic circuits for basic builtin operations (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
We develop arithmetic circuits for the set of basic builtin operations. These operations include all UPLC builtin operations from the latest specification, except cryptographic operations (blake2b_224, blake2b_256, sha2, sha3, BLS12_381 elliptic curve operations), conversions between integers and bytestrings, and the serialiseData operation.
・Arithmetic circuits for basic builtin operations (Haskell) can be found in our repo
ms.report:
We have completed the milestone as promised. The code is open-source and is published on our GitHub:

・https://github.com/zkFold/symbolic/blob/main/symbolic-uplc/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/UPLC/Evaluation.hs#L399
